Sarah: Anytime, Tom. Your hardware is fine, so just let the fallback pool carry the work until Harlo answers again.

Ping me here if anything looks off after you recon

messages.text: well it is cool so far. I got some bolt point stacking up already. I put harlo os on my gamma 601 so i can get the spins. I noticed today that my gamma was showing low hashrate of 2xxxghs on the site stats but my gamma 601 was at 1.4ths in the devies dash. Also i had 3 nano3 non s running sing the beginning and they also stopped hashing but at 0% so i pointed them 3 back to my node to hash.

Hi Tom, Hal here, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Short version first, then the one thing I need from you.

**Why the two numbers disagree**
1. Your device dashboard reports what the ASIC is actually doing right now (1.4 TH/s on the Gamma 601, that is normal for a 601 on Harlo OS).
2. The pool page does not measure your hashrate. It estimates it from the shares you submit over a window (usually 10 min to 1 h). On a sub-2 TH/s miner the share count per window is small, so that estimate swings a lot: it can read half or double your real rate and only settles over several hours. The 24 h average is the one to trust, not the live tile.
3. So a Gamma sitting at 1.4 TH/s locally while the site shows anything from a few hundred GH/s to 2+ TH/s is the estimator wobbling, not lost work. What actually matters is accepted shares climbing and rejects staying near zero.

**The N. 3s at 0% is a different thing.** 0% with no shares is usually a stratum drop (worker disconnected or re-auth failed) or the pool's minimum difficulty being too high for a device that small, so it can go a very long time without landing a share and shows as dead.

One question so I can tell which one it was: on the pool page, did those 3 Nano 3s ever show accepted shares at the start and then stop, or were they at 0 from the moment you pointed them at the Harlo pool?

Also tell me which Harlo OS version the Gamma 601 is on (UI, System page) and I will check it against the current release.

I had them all connected yesterday so they been running fine since then showing closely th same hashrates even the nanos. !.5ths to 200ghs in the site is too big of a diff to be just leveling out and they been running almost 24hrs now. I know iin beginning it can show low until they equal out. My nanos also been fin all that time until today around 1:15 today the sites charts sho them 3 going to zero and the gamma also at around that time wen down to 200ghs.

That changes the picture, and I agree with you: 1.5 TH/s local against 200 GH/s on the site after 24 h is not the estimator settling.

The important detail is that all four devices, three Nano 3s and the Gamma, went down at the same moment (around 1:15). Four independent miners do not fail together. That points at one of two things: something between you and the pool (router, DHCP lease, ISP hiccup, stratum disconnect) or something on the pool side at that time.

One check on the Gamma, since it is the one still pointed at the Harlo pool:

1. Open the Gamma web UI and look at the pool/stats section.
2. Tell me three numbers: accepted shares, rejected shares, and whether it shows a live pool connection (and the time of the last accepted share if it is listed).

If the accepted count is still climbing steadily and rejects are near zero, your miner is fine and the problem is on the pool's accounting side. If accepted stopped climbing or rejects are rising fast, it is a stratum or difficulty issue and I will fix it from there.

In parallel I am putting this in front of JD, who runs the Harlo pool, since he can see whether anything happened pool side around 1:15 today.
Handed to the team · Possible pool-side stats/stratum issue on the Harlo BCH pool; only JD can see th

JD has been pinged and someone from the team can jump into this chat. If you step away, you will get the answer by email.

Faster route if you want it now: the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate (JD). He is very active there and can look at the pool backend directly, and a timestamp like "around 1:15 PM ET today, four workers to zero" is exactly what he needs.

Send me those share numbers from the Gamma when you have them and we will keep going.

i already powered them off and on so the stats on the devices have been reset. I also have 2 NQ++ rev 6.1 and a Bs-2 that have not been effected at all. Those do not have harlo os on them ... only the gamma 601 has harlo os to get the free spins.

Counters resetting is no problem, they rebuild within minutes of hashing. Watch them fresh.

That new detail is the useful one though, and it narrows things down. If the NQ++ pair and the BS-2 are on the same network and were never affected, your router and internet are almost certainly fine. Which leaves the pool side.

One question, and it is the one that settles it:

Are the two NQ++ 6.1 and the BS-2 pointed at the Harlo BCH pool too, or at a different pool / your own node?

- If they are on a different pool or your node, then everything that broke was on the Harlo pool and nothing else was, so it is pool side.
- If they are on the Harlo pool and kept hashing normally through 1:15, then it is specific to the affected workers (their worker names, their assigned difficulty, or the stratum connection those units held), not the pool as a whole.

Worth noting as well: the Nano 3s do not run Harlo OS, so Harlo OS itself is not the common factor. The pool is.

While you check that, let the Gamma run 15 to 20 minutes and then tell me the accepted and rejected share counts plus what the site shows for it. That gives JD a clean before/after.
the divices have gone to the secondary pools so i think the pool is having issues bc the pool site wont show as normal

That is solid evidence, and I would read it the same way.

Automatic failover to the secondary pool means the miners themselves judged the primary stratum unreachable or not responding, and they only do that after the connection actually fails. Combine that with four workers dropping at the same minute and the pool site not rendering normally, and it is a pool-side problem, not your hardware, your network or Harlo OS.

What I would do for now:

1. Leave the devices on the fallback pool so they keep hashing instead of sitting idle.
2. Leave the Harlo pool configured as primary. Both Harlo OS and the stock NerdQaxe/Bitaxe firmware retry the primary and switch back on their own once it answers again, so there is nothing to reflash or reconfigure.
3. Do not factory reset anything. The config is not the problem.

Your diagnosis is already in front of JD with the 1:15 timestamp, and I have added that the units failed over on their own. For live status he is the fastest route: Discord https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate. Pool incidents usually get called out there first.

One thing I cannot speak to: how shares and bolt points are treated for the window the pool was down. That is JD's call, so ask him directly in the same message and he can tell you properly.
being a new poos site i expected some issues so this is not a surprise. I will check back to see if it is up and reset my devices back to it and see how it goes then thanks

Thanks for being patient with it, and for the clean report. Four workers dropping at the same minute plus automatic failover is exactly the kind of detail that makes a pool issue easy to pin down, so that was genuinely useful.

Two small things for when you point them back:

1. If the Gamma already has the Harlo pool as primary, you do not need to touch it. It will reconnect on its own once the stratum answers.
2. Give it 30 to 60 minutes before judging the site number against your device number. The pool estimate needs that many shares before it tracks your real rate, especially for the Nano 3s.

Your report is with JD, and the Discord (https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, @nullhashrate) is where pool status gets posted first. Good luck with the spins, and come back here if anything looks off once you are reconnected.
ok, the site now says "Cannot reach the pool status API. Any values shown are from the last successful update. Retrying automatically" so i guess they are working on the site.

That banner is the confirmation, and it explains the numbers you were seeing earlier.

What it means: the dashboard cannot reach the pool's status API, so every figure on the page is a frozen snapshot from the last successful update. That is exactly why your Gamma showed 200 GH/s while the device itself was at 1.4 TH/s, and why the three Nano 3s flatlined to zero at the same minute. Those were not four miners failing, they were one stale cache.

Two notes so you read it right when it comes back:

1. The status API and the stratum endpoint are separate pieces. Your miners failing over says stratum was affected too, not just the display. So the site recovering first does not automatically mean the mining endpoint is back.
2. The real test is your device UI: once it shows a live pool connection and the accepted share count climbing, you are genuinely mining to Harlo again, whatever the site says.

Nothing for you to do but wait on it. It is with JD, and Discord (https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, @nullhashrate) is where recovery gets announced first. Ping me here if it comes back up and the numbers still look wrong.

Anytime, Tom. Your hardware is fine, so just let the fallback pool carry the work until Harlo answers again.

Ping me here if anything looks off after you reconnect, and enjoy the spins.
